purpose: Change one length requirement and see which known strips witness an existential claim or refute a universal claim.
meaning: A quantifier combines a predicate with a domain. A universal statement says every domain element satisfies the predicate; an existential statement says at least one does. A witness establishes an existential statement, while a counterexample refutes a universal one. The same predicate can therefore make “some” true while “all” is false.

definition.setting: Universal and existential quantification over the complete finite nonempty domain of six stated strip lengths.
definition.formal_latex: D=\{2,4,6,8,10,12\}\,\mathrm{cm},\quad P(x):x\ge h;\quad \forall x\in D\ P(x),\quad \exists x\in D\ P(x).

signature.x: A strip length ranging over D.
signature.∃x∈D P(x): At least one strip meets the requirement.

conditions: The complete domain D consists of six known strip lengths: 2,4,6,8,10 and 12 cm. Every strip is included in the check.
The free parameter h is a real required length from zero to fourteen centimetres. The predicate P(x) is x≥h, including equality.
The universal statement is true if all six elements satisfy P. The existential statement is true if at least one satisfies P; “some” does not mean “some but not all”.
This finite nonempty domain permits a complete enumeration. An animation of these six cases does not establish a claim over all real numbers or an unspecified domain.
